text.title: Activation Framework Failure Modes
text.summary: Six antipatterns observed when applying Activation Framework. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix. Detector clauses make them mechanically catchable.

antipattern.symptom: Spec defines activation as "user experiences value" or lists three events joined by "or"; two analysts compute different activation rates from the same data.
antipattern.root-cause: Event chosen by narrative rather than by a tracked event name and a window.
antipattern.fix: Rewrite per rule `r-single-activation-event-with-window`: one event name, one window in days from signup. Reject the spec until the event can be pasted into a query.

antipattern.symptom: Activation rate climbs for six weeks; D30 retention does not move.
antipattern.root-cause: Event picked because it is easy to push users into (e.g. "profile completed"), never checked against D30 retention.
antipattern.fix: Build the comparison table required by `r-event-validated-against-d30-retention`; replace the event if the retained versus non-retained gap is negligible.

antipattern.symptom: Baseline shows a sharp drop in the most recent one or two weeks; the team opens an incident for a regression that does not exist.
antipattern.root-cause: Cohorts whose activation window has not elapsed included in the baseline and dashboard.
antipattern.fix: Apply `r-baseline-before-experiments` and `r-dashboard-reports-closed-cohorts-weekly`: exclude any cohort where signup date plus window exceeds the data cutoff.

antipattern.symptom: Funnel map lists eight steps; the warehouse has events for four of them; drop-off numbers exist for all eight.
antipattern.root-cause: Steps inferred from screens instead of from tracked events; missing figures filled by estimation.
antipattern.fix: Mark unmapped steps `uninstrumented` per `r-funnel-steps-map-to-events`, add instrumentation tasks, remove the estimated figures.

antipattern.symptom: Top drop-off priority is a step reached by a few dozen users per week; the step losing hundreds sits fourth.
antipattern.root-cause: Ranking on relative drop without absolute users lost.
antipattern.fix: Re-rank by absolute loss per `r-dropoffs-ranked-by-absolute-loss`, showing the relative drop as a secondary column.

antipattern.symptom: Two people re-score the backlog and the order changes; scores include values like 7.5 or 12.
antipattern.root-cause: Dimensions scored on different scales or weighted informally; no shared formula.
antipattern.fix: Score integers 1-10 and compute with `templates/ice.py` per `r-ice-integer-scale-and-formula`; record the three inputs, not only the result.
